meta.title: Black Creek Water Resource Development Project
meta.leadAgency: St. Johns River Water Management District (SJRWMD)
meta.location: Southwest Clay County, between Penney Farms and Camp Blanding

statedPrimaryPurpose.value: Increase recharge to the Upper Floridan aquifer in northeast Florida using excess flow from Black Creek. Lake restoration (Lake Brooklyn, Lake Geneva) is stated by SJRWMD as a SECONDARY benefit, not the primary purpose — do not characterize this as a "save the lakes" project.

scope.value: Diverts up to 10 million gallons/day from the South Fork of Black Creek during wet-weather high-flow periods, treats for color/nutrients, and discharges into Alligator Creek, which flows into Lake Brooklyn, enhancing aquifer recharge. Components: a pump station, a ~17-mile 30-inch pipeline, and a color-removal treatment system.

costEstimates.label: Current/revised construction cost estimate (pump station + pipeline + treatment system)
costEstimates.notes: The records reviewed establish the change in project cost (approximately $41M in 2017 to approximately $118.7M today, both figures from SJRWMD's own materials), but the specific causes of the increase (inflation, scope changes, land/easement costs, treatment-system addition, or something else) have not yet been established in this dataset. A records request to SJRWMD would be needed to confirm the breakdown.

legislativeSponsors2017.value: Sen. Rob Bradley (R-Fleming Island), Rep. Bobby Payne (R-Palatka), Rep. Travis Cummings (R-Orange Park)
legislativeSponsors2017.notes: Rob Bradley — NOT Jennifer Bradley, the later Senate sponsor of the FY2026-27 Clay County LFIR requests (see data/state-funding.json). Do not conflate the two Bradleys; any relationship between them was not independently confirmed and is not stated here.

clayCountyGovernmentConnection.value: Clay County Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved a perpetual easement on ~3 acres of county-owned property near SR 16 and SR 21 on December 1, 2017, allowing SJRWMD to implement the project and construct related recreational facilities.
clayCountyGovernmentConnection.recordsNeeded: The actual BCC agenda item / minutes / recorded easement instrument for the December 1, 2017 vote (claycounty.novusagenda.com) was not pulled this pass.

timeline.event: Clay County BCC approves easement on county property for the project plus recreational access
Anticipated full system operation; as of this research pass, intermittent test pumping has occurred using completed treatment cells
